title: Rectal Biopsy, Duodenal Atresia and Malrotation

steps.tx: Sampling rectal lining with a suction capsule to check ganglion cells is **rectal suction biopsy**. Absent ganglion cells with thick nerve bundles confirm Hirschsprung disease. It avoids a full thickness biopsy under anaesthesia in most infants. Suction biopsy must sample at least 2 centimetres above the dentate line, because the lowest rectum normally lacks ganglion cells.
steps.say: Rectal suction biopsy confirms Hirschsprung disease by showing absent ganglion cells.

vis.caption: Rectal suction biopsy. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Complete blockage of the duodenum present at birth is **duodenal atresia**. Babies vomit bile within hours of the first feed. It associates strongly with Down syndrome and other congenital anomalies. About a third of babies with duodenal atresia have Down syndrome, so karyotype discussion follows stabilisation.
steps.say: Duodenal atresia blocks the duodenum at birth, causing early bilious vomiting, often with Down syndrome.

steps.tx: Two bubbles greet the radiologist on this newborn's film, and together they are nearly a diagnosis. Air fills the stomach and the first part of duodenum, then stops dead, the **double bubble sign** of duodenal atresia with no gas beyond. A third of these babies carry Down syndrome, so the film triggers cardiac and karyotype conversations alongside the surgical referral. Feeds are stopped, the stomach decompressed, and theatre planned once associated anomalies have had their say.
steps.say: A double bubble with no distal gas on the newborn film is duodenal atresia until proven otherwise.

vis.caption: Double bubble sign. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Two gas bubbles in stomach and duodenum on a plain film form the **double bubble sign**. No gas beyond them confirms complete obstruction. The film is diagnostic enough to plan surgery after stabilisation. Gas beyond the two bubbles means atresia is incomplete, as in a duodenal web, and changes the operation planned.
steps.say: The double bubble sign shows stomach and duodenal gas with nothing beyond in duodenal atresia.

steps.tx: Failure of normal bowel rotation and fixation during development is **malrotation**. The narrow mesenteric base lets the whole midgut twist dangerously. Most present in the first month with bilious vomiting. Ladd bands cross the duodenum from the malpositioned caecum and can obstruct it even without a twist.
steps.say: Malrotation leaves a narrow mesenteric base that lets the midgut twist dangerously.

steps.tx: The operation untwisting the bowel, dividing bands and widening the mesentery is the **Ladd procedure**. The appendix is usually removed because its future position would confuse diagnosis. Bowel is laid in a safe non rotated position. The mesenteric base is widened so the bowel sits with small bowel on the right and colon on the left.
steps.say: The Ladd procedure untwists bowel, divides bands and widens the mesentery safely.

steps.tx: Bilious vomiting in a newborn is malrotation with volvulus until excluded, a rule of **urgent exclusion**. Upper gastrointestinal contrast shows the abnormal duodenal course. Any delay risks losing the entire midgut. A contrast study in a sick newborn should not wait for morning lists; senior teams image and operate at night.
steps.say: Bilious vomiting in a newborn is volvulus until excluded because delay risks the entire midgut.

steps.tx: Screening for associated anomalies after duodenal atresia includes cardiac and chromosomal assessment, termed **associated anomaly workup**. Heart defects are the most important to find before anaesthesia. Kidney and vertebral anomalies also occur. An echocardiogram before theatre is mandatory, because a duct dependent heart lesion changes anaesthetic planning completely.
steps.say: Associated anomaly workup after duodenal atresia checks heart, chromosomes and kidneys before anaesthesia.

steps.tx: **VACTERL association** is diagnosed when three or more of vertebral defects, anal atresia, cardiac malformations, tracheo oesophageal fistula, renal anomalies and radial limb defects coexist. A neonate with duodenal atresia still needs that associated anomaly workup before theatre. Heart defects matter most: an echocardiogram is mandatory, because a duct dependent lesion changes anaesthetic planning, while kidneys and vertebrae are checked in the same sitting.
steps.say: VACTERL association is diagnosed when three or more of vertebral defects, anal atresia, cardiac malformations, tracheo oesophageal fistula, renal anomalies and radial limb defects coexist. A neonate with duodenal atresia still needs that associated anomaly workup before theatre. Heart defects matter most: an echocardiogram is mandatory, because a duct dependent lesion changes anaesthetic planning, while kidneys and vertebrae are checked in the same sitting.

vis.alt: Cluster of vertebral, anal, cardiac, tracheo oesophageal, renal and radial limb anomalies grouped as VACTERL
vis.caption: Three or more of the VACTERL anomalies are shown together, including heart, kidney, vertebral and limb defects. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Feeding after duodenal repair often needs patience because the dilated stomach recovers slowly, called **functional delay**. Nasojejunal feeding or intravenous nutrition bridges the gap. Most babies progress to full feeds over weeks. The dilated proximal duodenum is sometimes tapered at surgery to help it empty after the join heals.
steps.say: Functional delay after duodenal repair needs bridging nutrition while the stomach recovers.

steps.tx: Anorectal anomalies frequently accompany duodenal and rotation problems under the umbrella of **VACTERL association**. Vertebral, cardiac, tracheal, renal and limb defects cluster together. Finding one anomaly mandates searching for others. The letters stand for vertebral, anal, cardiac, tracheo oesophageal, renal and limb defects, and three or more define the association.
steps.say: VACTERL association clusters anomalies, so finding one mandates searching for others.
